Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's first-inning effort as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The Australian players are in a huddle for a few last-minute instructions before taking their respective positions on the field. Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill will open the inning for India and will want to get their side off to a good start. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's go...
... SECOND INNING ...

Australia have been bowled out for 469! Having begun the day at the overnight score of 327-3, they have added 142 runs losing 7 wickets in the process. Steven Smith and Travis Head began the day on a positive note with the former reaching the three-figure mark in the very first over. After they managed to get rid of Travis Head, India adjusted their lines and lengths well and kept chipping in with wickets at regular intervals. Despite the frequent loss of wickets, Australian batters were able to keep the scoreboard ticking. Alex Carey was playing a fine knock and when he was out in the middle, Australia were on course for an even bigger total. However, Ravindra Jadeja was brought into the attack and he delivered by dismissing Carey. The tailenders did not shy away from playing their shots but they were unable to keep the Indians out in the field for much longer. The conditions are still good for batting and the onus will be on the Indian openers to see off the new ball. Stick around as India's reply is coming up shortly...

OUT! CAUGHT! Mohammed Siraj takes the last wicket and that brings an end to the Australian inning! This is a pretty good fightback from India after having a difficult Day 1 as they have claimed 7 wickets in about one and a half sessions. This is bowled back of a length and outside the off pole. Pat Cummins looks to make room by moving to the leg side and tries to slap the ball away. He ends up hitting this straight down the throat of Ajinkya Rahane at cover. Mohammed Siraj ends with four wickets and India still have some hope in this game. Australia will be disappointed in being bowled out before Tea after the position there were in when the day started.

Commentary.Commentary: The post-Lunch session is about to commence as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. Alex Carey and Pat Cummins stride out to the centre followed by the Indian players. Umesh Yadav will start the proceedings with the ball for India. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

After a great effort with the bat on Day 1, Travis Head and Steven Smith picked up where they left off and it took only two balls for the latter to reach his hundred. At the other end, Travis Head was at his fluent best and brought up his 150 before departing. Once this partnership was broken, Australia lost their way a bit by losing wickets at regular intervals. Alex Carey and Pat Cummins then joined hands and safely negotiated the remaining passage of play in the first session. Despite the loss of four wickets in the session, Australia scored at a brisk rate and will be hoping to frustrate the Indians with some fight by the tail in the second session. Can they succeed in doing so? We shall find out soon as the players return for the second session at 5.40 pm IST (12.10 pm GMT).

SESSION SUMMARY - 95 runs, 24 overs, 4 wickets. Having failed to win even a single session on Day 1, the first session on Day 2 has belonged to India. After a tough Day 1 with the ball, India were expected to fight back on Day 2 but could not set the tone early as they consistently missed their lines and lengths, allowing the two Australian batters to get their eye in. Mohammed Siraj's short-ball ploy to Travis Head eventually worked, giving India hope. It was then Mohammad Shami who dismissed the dangerous Cameron Green cheaply.  As he always does, Shardul Thakur struck gold for India, accounting for Steven Smith before Axar Patel's brilliance in the field removed Mitchell Starc. As India return after Lunch, they will be hoping to wrap up the innings as quickly as possible.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS - The Indian pace bowlers did not start well feeding Steven Smith with some easy deliveries to rush to his century. They did get things right eventually and it resulted in the wicket of Travis Head after he crossed 150 but the scoring rate has been pretty high in the first hour. Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The Indian players are in a huddle around the match ball before taking their respective positions on the field. Steven Smith and Travis Head stride out to the middle and will look to build on their 251-run partnership. Mohammed Siraj has the ball in his hand which is relatively new and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Nasser Hussain is pitchside and he says that the weather is really nice for cricket. Adds that at this time on Day 1, it was cloudy but it is sunny right now. Mentions that it was tough to bat early in the first session but got easier through the day. He is joined by Kumar Sangakkara who claims that it is easy to get strayed by the heavy cover of grass but it is tufty and with the indentations on the pitch, it is likely to hold the ball. Adds that it caused the ball to sit up early in the game and as the game progressed it stayed a bit low. Reckons that on Day 3, Day 4, and Day 5 it will spin as it is dry under all the grass. Ends by saying that Ravindra Jadeja will try to target the rough and with the Australian pace bowlers pounding on the pitch, the spinners will definitely come into play with footmarks to play with.

On the other hand, India were off to a perfect start, with Mohammed Siraj and Mohammad Shami setting the tone for them. India even managed to reduce Australia to 76-3, but they were unable to keep the pressure on. They kept offering freebies to the opposition batters and now face the uphill task of restricting Australia. With the ball still relatively new, India will be hoping to make some early inroads in the first session. Can India fight their way back into the game? We shall find out soon, as the first ball on Day 2 is not far away.

After being put in to bat under overcast conditions, Australia were dealt an early blow as Usman Khawaja departed without troubling the scorers. David Warner and Marnus Labuschagne applied themselves well and cashed in later, when shot making became easier. Both batters departed on either side of the Lunch break, but Travis Head and Steven Smith got together and put their side in a commanding position. With conditions still good for batting, Australia will look to bat for as long as possible.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 2 of the 2021–23 World Test Championship final between Australia and India at the Kennington Oval in London. The opening day of the final certainly lived up to expectations, and it was Australia who dominated all three sessions to take the ascendancy at the end of Day 1.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

A day that has belonged to Australia and they will be eager to press their advantage further on Day 2. India will feel like they allowed this match to slip out of their hands and will have to regroup in order to come back in this game. The action continues on Thursday 8th June as we shall have Day 2 of this ultimate Test match and the first ball will be bowled at 3 pm IST (9.30 am GMT) but do join us early for the build-up. Cheers!

The man of the moment for Australia, Travis Head is in for a chat after scoring the first century in a World Test Championship final. He says that it is an exceptionally good job after losing the toss this morning. Mentions that there is still plenty of help with the second new ball. Adds that they need to do a lot of hard work on Day 2. Shares that he was trying to get into good positions. Also says that it was testing times but he tried to work and adjust his way through those periods. Ends by saying that it feels nice to have a batter at the other end playing well as he was.

Rohit Sharma cited the conditions for electing to bowl first which they haven't done since 2015 but the pacers found help only in the first hour of play. Mohammed Siraj managed to dismiss Usman Khawaja on a duck but Marnus Labuschagne and David Warner put on a 69-run partnership to negotiate the new ball and take their team to a decent position. Warner departed just before Lunch as he gloved a leg-side delivery from Shardul Thakur to the keeper but the first session still belonged to the Aussies. Mohammad Shami struck early in the second session dismissing the number one Test batter Marnus Labuschagne but after that, it has been all Australia as they went into Tea without losing any more wickets. The last session established their dominance as they did not lose a single wicket and the unbeaten 251-run partnershiop between Steven Smith and Travis Head has made this their game to lose.

SESSION SUMMARY - 157 runs, 34 overs, 0 wickets. A session that has been absolutely dominated by the Australians as they have scored at a rapid rate and taken this game away from the Indians. They came into this final part of Day 1 looking to take the initiative and have done so successfully courtesy of an outstanding century by Travis Head who reached the landmark in just 106 balls. His batting effort took the wind out of the sails of the Indian bowlers as they looked completely ineffective with the sun out. Steven Smith showed us there was still a lot of value in playing a traditional Test match inning as he held up one end showing loads of grit and determination to preserve his wicket. He remains unbeaten and is 5 runs short of his century while Head is eyeing a double century having scored 146 runs in 156 deliveries. India have clearly misjudged these conditions and they would have liked to turn to Ravichandran Ashwin in such a situation but will now have to play out of their skins to turn the tie back in their favor.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session on Day 1. Out come the two umpires followed by the Indian players. Steven Smith and Travis Head will resume the innings for Australia. Umesh Yadav will start the proceedings with the ball for India. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

India needed wickets early and would have felt absolutely pumped up when Mohammad Shami grabbed one on his very first delivery of this session. They would have liked to press their advantage forward at that time but the bowlers lacked the required discipline to keep things tight. They served far too many loose deliveries and allowed the opponents to score freely which released all the pressure that they had built. The introduction of Ravindra Jadeja caused a few problems for the batters and the Indians may be left wondering if it was a good idea for them to leave out the number one Test bowler as they continue to struggle to get timely wickets. The last session of Day 1 could set the framework for this game as Australia could run away with this tie or India could come roaring back with a bunch of wickets. Do join us at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT) to find out how the last session plays out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 97 runs, 28 overs, 1 wicket. Another session that has belonged to the Aussies as they have scored at a brisk rate post Lunch and with seven wickets in hand, they are well on course to reach a good first-inning total. After negotiating the difficult pitch in the first session they looked to build on their start but were pegged back when they lost Marnus Labuschagne right after the break. Travis Head walked out to the middle and did not allow the pressure to build as he played his natural game to counterattack the Indian pace bowlers. It worked perfectly well for them as Steven Smith provided the resistance at the other end playing the perfect anchor role. They put together a 94-run unbeaten partnership for the fourth wicket with Head reaching his half-century in just 60 deliveries. They will look to continue the good work after Tea and take complete control of this game.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session. The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the two Australian batters. The Indian players stride out to the centre and take their respective field positions. Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne will resume the innings for Australia. Mohammed Siraj will start the proceedings with the ball for India. Off we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

As far as India are concerned, they did manage to dismiss David Warner in the penultimate over before Lunch but they will be a bit disappointed with their bowling effort. It was Mohammed Siraj who set the tone early by dismissing Usman Khawaja in his second over. Mohammad Shami kept it tight at his end as well by bowling probing lines and lengths. That said, India had only one wicket to show for their efforts in the first hour. After the drinks break, Umesh Yadav and Shardul Thakur were brought into the attack to give the frontline bowlers a rest. However, Umesh was unable to find his line and length and leaked a lot of runs in his first few overs. The move to persist with Thakur worked wonders for India as he delivered big time by dismissing Warner. India would have wanted a wicket or two more but they will be hoping to start well after Lunch.  Another entertaining session of cricket awaits us, so do join us back at 5.40 pm IST (12.10 pm GMT)

SESSION SUMMARY - 73 runs, 23 overs, 2 wickets. An absorbing session of Test cricket comes to an end and one would feel that it will be Australia who will be the happier of the two sides going into the break. After Rohit Sharma called it right and put Australia into bat, they were rocked early, losing Usman Khawaja in the 4th over. David Warner struggled initially but he found good support at the other end from Marnus Labuschagne. The duo showed good application in overcast conditions and safely negotiated the tricky first hour. As the session progressed, batting became easier and both batters started to settle into the groove by finding boundaries. However, Warner departed just before Lunch and now the onus is on Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne to take the innings forward after Lunch.
A dot ball to end the session! This is served full and outside the off stump. Marnus Labuschagne gets his front foot forward and defends this solidly towards cover. That will be LUNCH on DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the prematch formalities as we are set for the final to get underway and the umpires walk towards the center. The Indian players are in a huddle for a few last-minute instructions from Rohit Sharma before taking their respective positions on the field. David Warner and Usman Khawaja will open the inning for Australia and will want to negotiate the new ball in difficult conditions. Mohammad Shami has the brand new cherry in his hand and will begin proceedings. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game. The Test Mace is being taken out to the middle as the two sets of players walk out and lineup for their respective national anthems. However, before that, there will a minute of silence for all the people who lost their lives in the train crash in Odisha. We will now have the Indian national anthem followed by the national anthem of Australia.

Pat Cummins, the captain of Australia says that they would have bowled first as well but it shouldn’t make much of a difference and hopefully, they can get some spin on Day 4 and 5. Informs that they are going with Scott Boland, Mitchell Starc, and himself as the fast bowlers. Claims that this pitch should suit Boland and with a bit of grass he will be a weapon for them. Mentions that they have been here for 10 days with some playing county cricket for longer so they are pretty fresh.

Rohit Sharma, the skipper of India, says that they will bowl first. Feels that the decision is based on the overhead conditions and reckons that the pitch will not change much. Informs that they are going with four seamers and one spinner in the form of Ravindra Jadeja. Shares that leaving Ravichandran Ashwin out of the side, who has been a match-winner, is tough. Adds that you got to do the things that are needed for the team. On Ajinkya Rahane's return, he says that Rahane brings a lot to the table and has the experience of playing in these conditions.
India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Cheteshwar Pujara, Virat Kohli, Ajinkya Rahane, KS Bharat (WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Shardul Thakur, Umesh Yadav, Mohammad Shami, Mohammed Siraj.
Australia (Playing XI) - David Warner, Usman Khawaja, Marnus Labuschagne, Steven Smith, Travis Head, Cameron Green, Alex Carey (WK), Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins (C), Nathan Lyon, Scott Boland.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of India. They have elected to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Kumar Sangakkara and Dinesh Karthik are pitchside. Sangakkara informs that it is overcast and expects the ball to swing. Adds that there is a good covering of grass and there will be good bounce as well. Looking at the pitch and overhead conditions, Karthik feels that the captain winning the toss will opt to bowl first. Reckons that India will go with four pacers and adds that a lot of cricket will be played on the first three days where pacers will come into play.

On the other hand, India, being one of the most successful Test sides in home and away conditions, lost only one out of the six series played during the two-year period. However, they have some key absentees, which gives others the opportunity to put their hands up in this all-important final. With this being the first Test played in June at this venue, if the surface starts to spin, the Rohit Sharma-led side would fancy themselves to conquer the Test. Folks, it is time to gear yourselves up for five days of enthralling Test cricket action. Which team will be in the ascendancy at the end of Day 1? Let’s find out. Australia made it to the final on the back of a dominant run that saw them lose only three out of the 19 Tests played during the World Test Championship cycle. The conditions at the Kennington Oval do suit Pat Cummins and Co., but they would be wary of India's recent Test success at this venue. Despite missing Josh Hazlewood, they have enough resources in the bowling unit to fill that void. With the bat, a lot will rely on Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne who have done well against India and also on Usman Khawaja who is in great form ever since his return.
